headline: Apple Wallet Digital ID may expand beyond passports, reports suggest
summary: Apple's Digital ID, currently used for US passports, is rumored to be expanding its functionality. This could introduce new ways to use your iPhone as official identification.
details: Apple debuted Digital ID on iPhone last year, initially allowing users to store their US passports in Apple Wallet. This feature aimed to provide a convenient and secure method for identity verification.

New reports indicate that Apple is exploring significant additional applications for its Digital ID system. This potential expansion could broaden the scope of how iPhones are used for official identification.

While specific details regarding these future use cases remain unconfirmed, the development suggests Apple's ongoing commitment to enhancing its digital identity solutions within the Wallet ecosystem.

headline_marked: [[Argentina launches CHE MCP]], its first national AI data gateway with 5-stage classifier
headline: Argentina launches CHE MCP, its first national AI data gateway with 5-stage classifier
summary: This intelligent gateway connects AI agents to 80+ official Argentine data sources in real-time, solving the need for multiple servers.
details: Argentina has unveiled CHE MCP, its first national Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem, developed in Bahía Blanca. This intelligent gateway allows any AI agent to access over 80 official Argentine data sources in real-time, including dollar exchange rates, weather, and tax compliance.

Currently, AI agents require individual MCP servers for each data source. CHE MCP streamlines this by providing a single server that understands natural language in Spanish and automatically routes queries to the correct data.

The system employs a 5-stage classifier to process queries. This includes keyword matching across 3,000+ keywords, Weighted Majority Algorithm (WMA) routing, semantic embeddings using 384-dim vectors, and a Data Node search over 748 Parquet datasets.

The Weighted Majority Algorithm (WMA) is an online learning system embedded in the router. It reinforces successful domains (+0.1 weight) and penalizes failures (−0.1 weight), ensuring the router continuously improves with every query.

CHE MCP achieved a 95.45% Top-First-Score accuracy on MCPAgentBench with 66 diverse queries. It utilizes 748 Parquet datasets from datos.gob.ar, Argentina's open data portal, compressed 9.92x from 3.92 GB CSV to 404 MB.

The Data Node converts natural language queries into DuckDB SQL, enabling direct interaction with the datasets. It includes SQL injection guardrails, read-only enforcement, a 5-second timeout, and a 1,000-row result limit.

The system is future-proofed for the Model Context Protocol's architectural update in July 2026, which mandates Streamable HTTP transport and stateless architecture. CHE MCP was designed with these requirements in mind from its inception, built with Gentle AI's SDD orchestration and Engram persistent memory.
